title: 22 Years Ago, Studio Ghibli’s Most Whimsical Anti-War Movie Was Released & It Holds Up Even Today
content:
Howl’s Moving Castle remains one of the most whimsical fantasies of all time, even 22 years after its premiere. Founded by directors Hayao Miyazaki and Isao Takahata and producer Toshio Suzuki in 1985, Studio Ghibli eventually became one of the most globally renowned animation studios of all time. The films created under the banner of the studio are known for captivating storytelling, deep emotional impact, visually striking animation, and more. One of Miyazaki’s most unforgettable works is still Howl’s Moving Castle , a fantasy film based on Diana Wynne Jones’ 1986 novel.

The acclaimed film was even nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature at the 78th Academy Awards. While fans have always debated over which is the best Ghibli film, there’s no denying that when it comes to fantasy themes and anti-war allegory, Howl’s Moving Castle stands out as the best among all of the studio’s previous works. It’s also a widely accepted opinion that the movie was even better than the original novel , which isn’t something fans are used to seeing. The movie hit the Japanese theatres on November 20th, 2004, and its legacy remains unmatched even today.

Howl’s Moving Castle Is More Than Just a Romance Fantasy

The story centers around Sophie, a young girl who encounters the famous wizard Howl and catches the eye of an evil witch. Fueled by jealousy, the Witch of the Waste curses Sophie to turn into a 90-year-old woman. She accepts her fate, and Sophie leaves her home without telling anyone so she wouldn’t end up being a burden to her family. She travels alone without any destination in mind and luckily manages to enter Howl’s Castle without an invitation. She begins working there as a maid, forming an unlikely bond with the residents, including Howl, as she gets entangled in the world of magic.

However, while the film presents itself as a romance fantasy, it’s celebrated even to this day due to its anti-war allegory, themes of pacifism, self-acceptance, and many layers of core themes that will make you want to rewatch this beloved classic again and again . Miyazaki is widely recognized as a pacifist, and his ideologies are often reflected in his movies. Howl’s Moving Castle portrays war without clearly showing any side as good or evil, and yet the senseless conflict continues to affect the lives of ordinary citizens.

Without any side to root for or any moral justification behind the war, the movie primarily focused on the brutalities of the war rather than showing a heroic tale. The people carried on with their lives despite the bombings as they became almost numb to the never-ending conflict. However, the most brutal depiction of the war was when Howl slowly began to lose his humanity after being forced to participate in the war. As a talented magician, he was forced to use his powers to cause destruction, which slowly made him turn into a monster. This is what sets the movie apart from other tales of war, and it’s the reason why it’s a timeless classic.

Has Howl’s Moving Castle stayed with you ever since you watched it? Which moment do you find yourself thinking about the most? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

title: Forgotten 1960s Shonen Classic Is Now Easier to Stream in the U.S. Than Ever
content:
Criterion is streaming one of the most iconic 1960s anime series that have been forgotten over the decades due to limitations in access. The history of the anime industry dates back several decades, but the medium finally began becoming popular in Japan during the 1950s and 1960s, thanks to the color theatrical features and the rise of TV animation. Several classics across all demographics were released during that era, and it goes without saying that Shonen was more popular than others even back then. However, while those series were pretty popular during the time of their broadcast, most of them couldn’t stand the test of time when it became increasingly difficult for fans to watch them later on.

This is especially true for fans in the U.S. since several older classics are difficult to watch even now. However, Criterion made it possible to stream Speed Racer , one of the most legendary anime shows of all time. While it isn’t an obscure show anymore, thanks to the Hollywood live-action adaptation by the Wachowski sisters in 2008, the anime itself has been difficult to watch for a while now. The official Instagram handle of the service revealed its December 2026 lineup, where Speed Racer was also listed. The handle confirms that the complete series will be available on the platform in both Japanese audio with subtitles and the English dub as well.

What Is Speed Racer About?

Based on an iconic manga written and illustrated by Tatsuo Yoshida, Speed Racer premiered in 1967 and ran for 52 episodes. The story centers around Go Mifune, who pilots the Mach 5, the name of the technologically advanced racing car built by his father, Pops Racer. The series doesn’t shy away from portraying the brutality of the world of professional racing as Go gets entangled with all kinds of underhanded plots of corrupt businessmen and obstacles set by his rivals.

The visuals and color palette might give the impression that it’s a kid’s show, but it handles mature themes that are suitable for viewers of all ages. Not to mention that the best part of the anime was that, unlike typical racing stories, it blends family drama, political intrigue, and automotive fantasy.

Speed Racer Was a Major Breakthrough Anime For Its Animation Studio

Established in 1962, Tatsunoko Production eventually became one of the oldest animation studios in Japan that’s relevant to this day. Over the decades, the animation studio has released more than 200 anime, including films and series. It’s known for several acclaimed shows, such as Ping Pong the Animation , Psycho-Pass , and many more.

The studio thrived during the 1970s and 1980s, when there wasn’t an endless stream of anime TV shows being released for global fans. However, its legacy is mostly thanks to the success of Speed Racer , which helped the studio gain a strong foothold in the industry not long after its establishment. The studio even released a reboot and spin-off in an attempt to keep this series relevant for the next few decades.

Have you heard of Speed Racer before? Head down to the comments to let us know if you will be watching the anime next month on Criterion.

title: South Park Teases Kenny’s Return in Season 29 Finale First Look – Watch New Trailer
content:
South Park is setting up for Kenny’s return in the first look at what is poised to be the grand finale for Season 29 coming in the next episode. South Park Season 29 kicked off its run earlier this year with some big changes to the formula. Not only did it change the name of the show and town to “South America,” but it also returned to form by killing off Kenny at the end of the premiere episode . But it seems like the series is going back on it now.

South Park Season 29 has now reached the end of its confirmed six episodes previously scheduled with Comedy Central with the final of these episodes making their debut on Wednesday, November 25th. It seems like the animated series is going all out for the occasion, and with the final episode now slated, Comedy Central has dropped the first look at what’s coming and you can check it out in action below.

South Park Season 29 Episode 6 Confirms Release Date & Time

South Park Season 29 Episode 6 is titled “City Endings” and will be making its debut with Comedy Central on Wednesday, November 25th at 10PM ET/PT before being available to stream exclusively with Paramount+ the next day in the United States, Canada and Australia. While the rest of the season had been hinging on some sort of reveal for Grand Theft Auto VI or the midterm elections , that doesn’t seem to be the case for this episode as it’s going to reference some more recent current events.

The synopsis for the episode teases it as such, “When mysterious power outages strike South America, the townspeople fear Chinese cyberattacks. It’s up to the boys to discover what’s really going on.” But with the previous episode seemingly moving away from the midterm election results (and likely Grand Theft Auto ) , it seems like creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone have figured out a new path forward. And that seems to involve Kenny in some way with the special preview image you can find below.

Is Kenny Returning in South Park Season 29?

South Park killed off Kenny at the start of the season, and even saw him replaced by a new little version of Randy for one of the episodes . But it seems like the finale is going to reset everything once more as this “City Ending” for the season will find a way to wrap up all of the stories that had been ongoing in a seemingly unsatisfying fashion. But that just seems like the joke at play, so we’ll have to see how it actually all works out as the season comes to an end.

There’s still a question amidst all of this, however, as South Park Studios’ deal with Paramount meant that Parker and Stone need to deliver at least ten episodes of the series a year over the course of five years. With this season seemingly capping off with six episodes, there could be an announcement for future scheduled episodes to come after this one airs. Or maybe a slate of new specials for the holidays.

What are you hoping to see in South Park Season 29’s potential finale? How have you liked the season so overall? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: Bleach’s Hell Arc Deserves to Return With New Sequel
content:
There’s still one final Bleach arc that’s left to tell its story, and fans deserve to see it come to fruition one day to continue from Tite Kubo’s original series. Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War ended its official anime run earlier this Fall to cap over 22 years of the anime franchise . This adapted the final arc of Kubo’s original manga, but that’s also far from the end of the story as it is. Because back in 2021, Kubo actually continued from that finale to start something new.

When Bleach was celebrating its 20th anniversary, that’s where it was first announced that the anime would be returning for a proper adaptation of Kubo’s final arc. But that wasn’t all as Kubo himself also came back to the pages of Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump with a new one-shot picking up from the original end of the story. Featuring an older Ichigo Kurosaki, introducing new characters, enemies and more, Bleach’ s Hell Arc really needs to be fleshed out with a full sequel.

What Is Bleach “No Breathes From Hell”?

Bleach “No Breathes From Hell” was a 75 page one-shot manga release that first launched in 2021, and picks up a few years after the original end of the series. Exploring more of the ten year time skip seen with the original finale, Kazui and Ichika have grown a bit older and more of the Soul Society rankings have filled out with the new one-shot introducing some new members to each squad. Kazui has grown much stronger, and the Soul Society is preparing for a special bit of funeral rites for the late Ukitake. But things get more complicated from there.

A massive skeletal being arrives with no one other than Ichika being able to sense it before it makes its move, and it’s revealed that these new monsters don’t have any spiritual pressure of their own. Soon enough, the formerly defeated Szayelaporro arrives and reveals that he was cast into Hell after his defeat. It’s a brand new region that has never been referenced before, and with it has granted him an entirely new level of dark power that seems to have given him godly new abilities.

Soul Society begins to get covered in a dark matter known as “Phosphoplasm” and an entire new class of beings is revealed. Beings with too strong spiritual pressure never return completely to the Soul Society and are said to have been sent somewhere else and thus cast into Hell. This includes former enemies and even former Soul Reapers that have died in battle. With the final pages of the one shot, Bleach kicks off the “New Breathes From Hell” arc with no signs of continuing after five long years.

Why Bleach’ s Hell Arc Needs to Continue

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War’ s anime finale has now put a final button on the story, but this one-shot remains a continuation that has yet to be touched even after five years of inactivity. This new sequel teases returns from not only some of those most memorable villains of the past, but also new and terrifying versions of each of the major fan favorite Soul Reapers that have died along the way. There’s even a potential to see some of the Soul Reapers that had never been even shown until they were teased in the anime like the first generation of fighters .

But after spending all this time to bring back Bleach through the anime, and even having Kubo continue the franchise’s story with a new one-shot and even the Burn the Witch spinoff series, there’s clearly an interest from the creator to keep messing around with the story . A new sequel would be the perfect way to keep it going, but there are also other potential issues that spring up as a result. That includes the potential schedule for which Kubo would need to abide by. That probably seems like the biggest hurdle to overcome, but not an impossible one.

Shueisha’s editorial department has worked with their notable creators before to work out a schedule that’s for the creators’ benefit like seen with Hunter x Hunter’ s Yoshihiro Togashi. They’ve already done that with Kubo’s work on Burn the Witch, so it’s possible that they could work out a new schedule that could allow this sequel to exist. Where it’s a big chapter coming out every few months, weekly, or even once a year, Bleach just needs to continue so we can see what’s next . Would you want to see more of Bleach’ s Hell Arc? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: Avatar: Seven Havens Producer Explains Why No Last Airbender or Korra Writers Return
content:
Avatar: Seven Havens introduces a new room of writers to the franchise, and the showrunner behind it all has explained why they decided against bringing back any of the writers from Avatar: The Last Airbender or The Legend of Korra. The new era of the franchise has been a big success with Paramount+ thus far as the first season of the series has done well with both critics and fans . And much of that success has been thanks to the fact it feels so fresh.

Avatar: Seven Havens not only introduces an entirely different kind of art style and animation than seen with its predecessors , but the writers behind the series are all new as well. When asked about the choice to not bring back any of the writers from the older shows in a recent Reddit AMA , executive producer Sehaj Sethi explained that they “wanted to create a room with new voices who I felt could really flesh out these new characters.” It was a deliberate choice to go this route.

Why Avatar: Seven Havens Doesn’t Bring Back Any Previous Writers

“While I deeply respect and admire all the writers on the previous two series, I wanted to create a room with new voices who I felt could really flesh out these new characters,” Sehaji explained about the approach to Avatar: Seven Havens ‘ writing. “We had racial and gender parity between all the writers, and I think that really helped bring a lot of depth and complexity to the storytelling.” But even if the episodes don’t have previous show writers , the franchise has been overseen by the original creators.

When putting Avatar: Seven Havens together, Sehaj revealed that original franchise creators Michael DiMartino and Bryan Konietzko already had the idea of setting it within a post-apocalyptic world in mind . “Mike and Bryan approached me with this concept already in mind,” the producer began. “I think they had been noodling with setting the next series far into the future for a while. There were definitely challenges to creating seven brand new, unique city-states and cultures, but it was also freeing to be able to bring a lot of new ideas and concepts to the franchise.”

Avatar: Seven Havens Won’t Repeat the Mistakes of the Past

Avatar: Seven Havens has also been put together in a much more concrete way than with The Legend of Korra too. DiMartino previously explained that unlike its predecessor where it was initially planned out to have just a single season for its story, Avatar: Seven Havens has been developed with a clear end goal in mind from the start . While the number of seasons didn’t really settle until Paramount+ gave the all clear, the team had an idea of where they were going and how to get there.

Avatar: Seven Havens has confirmed that it will eventually come to an end with four seasons under its belt. Season 2 of the animated series is currently scheduled to make its debut with Paramount+ next May, and Season 3 will then follow later in 2027. The fourth season has yet to confirm a release date or window as of this time, but at least fans can rest easy knowing that this team has a firm plan in mind. But how are you feeling about Avatar: Seven Havens ‘ writing so far? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

title: Major Shonen Jump Series Creator Kicks Off New Return With Special Crossover
content:
One major creator has returned to the pages of Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine only a year after their previous series came to an end, and has kicked things off with a special crossover to help celebrate. Shonen Jump has entered its final transitional period for the year as a number of titles have kicked off their own serializations as fans say goodbye to some of the longer running hits . But with this go around, some of these new titles are from experienced creators.

Hitsuji Gondaira wrapped up Mission: Yozakura Family ‘s run with Shonen Jump last year , and has already made his return to the magazine with the start of a new series. Making its debut over the weekend, Hizuki of the Ginza Patrol offers a much different kind of story than seen with the chaotic spy adventures of Gondaira’s previous work. As a special way to celebrate the new debut, Gondaira has released a special crossover with Hizuki and Taiyo joining the Ginza Patrol. Check it out below.

Hizuki of the Ginza Patrol Creator Shares Mission: Yozakura Family Crossover

Hizuki of the Ginza Patrol made its full debut with Shonen Jump this past weekend , and the first chapter of the new series offers an entirely different kind of story than fans had seen with Mission: Yozakura Family. While that series offered an extended cast as Taiyo joined a huge family of spies, this new series doesn’t go that route. Instead fans are introduced to Osamu Hizuki, a samurai who’s come out of the war with the intent of living a life enjoying the new era and its technologies.

Hizuki of the Ginza Patrol already seems a lot more focused when it comes to its core cast as there’s really only Hizuki and his new partner Rin. She’s the first girl to join the patrol, and is only doing so to eventually solve the murder of her mother. Hizuki was one of the most deadly samurai in the war, but hopes to leave that life behind eventually and enjoy his new life. We’ll see how this all develops as the series hopefully gets the chance to have as long of a run as Mission: Yozakura Family was able to before it ended .

Will Hizuki of the Ginza Patrol Succeed With Shonen Jump ?

Shonen Jump is an incredibly fickle magazine as this year alone has already seen 14 different titles come to their ends. Only six of those releases were titles that were able to come to their natural conclusions , and all of the others had been cancelled shortly into their respective runs. It’s hard to tell at this point if Gondaira’s newest work has any real chance of success, but it’s likely to avoid cancellation at least for a while since it’s a returning creator already familiar with how Shonen Jump operates.

That’s not always the best thing for Shonen Jump , however, as even some returning creators have had their new works cancelled after short runs. It doesn’t matter how successful their prior work is either as with notable cases like Masashi Kishimoto’s Samurai 8 getting cancelled after a few months despite how big of a runaway hit Naruto was before. It’s all a toss up.

How are you feeling about Hizuki of the Ginza Patrol so far? Do you think it has a chance at success with Shonen Jump ? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: New Dark Fantasy Isekai Anime Confirms Crunchyroll Release Date With New Trailer – Watch
content:
A new dark fantasy Isekai anime is coming to Crunchyroll this January, and has now locked down its release date with a new trailer and poster showing it all off. With the ongoing slate of Fall 2026 anime releases now rounding out their respective final phases, it’s time to look ahead to all of the new releases coming our way next year. And 2027 looks like it’s going to be kicking things off on the right foot for Isekai anime fans with one series in particular.

The anime adaptation for Yu Shimizu and Makoto Aogiri’s Otherworldly Munchkin: Let’s Speedrun the Dungeon with Only 1 HP! was originally scheduled for a release in Fall 2025 before being hit by a major production delay behind the scenes. But it’s finally now set a release date of January 7th next year as part of the upcoming Winter 2027 slate. To commemorate the release of the new series, you can check out the new trailer and poster for the upcoming Isekai below.

Otherworldly Munchkin Isekai Confirms January 2027 Release Date

Otherworldly Munchkin: Let’s Speedrun the Dungeon with Only 1 HP! is currently scheduled to release in Japan on January 7th, and will be streaming exclusively with Crunchyroll when it finally makes its debut. There have been quite a few shake ups behind the scenes following its two year delay too with Naoya Fukushi now directing the series for Studio Durandal with Mamoru Yokota and Yui Kato providing the character designs, Yui Horiguchi serving as CG director, Hiroshi Hosokawa providing the scripts, and Asami Tachibana composing the music.

It’s also been confirmed that Otherworldly Munchkin: Let’s Speedrun the Dungeon with Only 1 HP! will feature the opening theme titled “Sai” as performed by LIL LEAGUE, and an ending theme titled “Zanka” as performed by ZAQ. Both of which have been previewed in this newly released trailer. The voice cast for the series includes Kazuki Ura as Yukito Kirihara, Kana Yuki as Charlotte R. Brownia, Yui Ishikawa as Lumilia Sherwood, Kaori Maeda as Liverna Dark, Hika Tsukishiro as Sana Kirihara, Fukushi Ochiai as Rocinante, Ayasa Ito as Managarmr, Yoko Hikasa as Nephilia Curse, Anri Katsu as the narrator, and Yuichiro Umehara as Sharaza.

What to Know for Otherworldly Munchkin

Otherworldly Munchkin: Let’s Speedrun the Dungeon with Only 1 HP! takes a dark path much like some of the Isekai anime releases that have gotten a lot of attention from fans in the last few years. Yukito and his sister are suddenly transported to another world, but he’s got a major disadvantage in exploring it. When he’s brought to this new world he’s given a mysterious character sheet and given all sorts of random properties by a mysterious woman.

Discovering he only has a single hit point, Yukito needs to navigate this mysterious new world and find his sister all while dealing with some strange new threats. There’s some of kind of underlying threat underneath it all, and that always leads to some great results with Isekai anime of this kind. With so many other new Isekai coming our way next year , what are you hoping to see in action in 2027? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: HIDIVE to Premiere Murciélago Anime at Anime Frontier Event in Texas
content:
HIDIVE announced on Monday that it will screen the world premiere of the anime of Kana Yoshimura 's Murciélago manga at this year's Anime Frontier convention on December 5 at 11:30 am CST, and also confirmed that it will stream the anime in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia, and New Zealand.

The company previously announced the North American premiere of the television anime of Nikumura Q 's Giant Ojō-sama (Giant Young Lady) manga at the same event on December 4. It will stream the series for the winter 2027 season in the U.S., Canada, the U.K., Ireland, Australia, and New Zealand.

HIDIVE will also screen the North American premiere of Made in Abyss: Awakening Mystery ( Made in Abyss: Mezameru Shinpi ), the first film in the new Made in Abyss anime film series , at Anime Frontier on December 5. HIDIVE will distribute the film in 2027.

The Murciélago anime will premiere on Japanese television in January 2027.

The Giant Ojō-sama anime will also premiere in January 2027.

The Made in Abyss: Awakening Mystery film opened in Japan on October 23.

Anime Frontier will run from December 4 to December 6 in Fort Worth, Texas.

title: Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End to Officially Return With New Spinoff Amid Hiatus
content:
Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End has unfortunately been on an indefinite hiatus for the past year with no signs of coming back anytime soon , but the series will be kicking off an official new spinoff series in the meantime. Kanehito Yamada and Tsukasa Abe’s original manga series originally made its debut with Shogakukan’s Weekly Shonen Sunday magazine in 2020, and has been a massive success ever since. Unfortunately, the series has gone on hiatus a number of times through its serialization thus far (with the latest being the longest yet).

As Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End continues through the manga’s hiatus that first kicked off last October , thankfully Shogakukan has now officially confirmed that there’s still something that fans can enjoy coming our way. Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End – Side Story has been announced as a “short term serialization” that will be highlighting even more of Heiter and Fern’s past than seen in the original series. Check out the announcement below.

Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End – Side Story Spinoff Officially Announced

Making its debut with the December 2nd issue of Shogakukan’s Weekly Shonen Sunday magazine, Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End – Side Story will see original artist Tsukasa Abe returning for this new spinoff. The first look at the series showcases Heiter and a young Fern, and teases we’ll see even more of their time together that we couldn’t see in the main series. This new spinoff is only going to be running for a short time, however, but a concrete end date or number of chapters have yet to be revealed as of the time of this initial announcement.

But with the original artist returning for this side story, it likely means that the main Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End is going to continue with its hiatus for much longer than fans might have expected. This year long wait has already been tough for many fans, but at least the release of this new spinoff means that there’s still going to be new materials to enjoy. Potential international releases for the spinoff have yet to be confirmed as of this announcement, but it’s certainly something to keep an eye on as it develops even further.

When Does Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End Season 3 Come Out?

While the manga is on a hiatus with no sights of returning anytime soon, the anime is getting ever closer to its own return. Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End Season 3 is currently scheduled to make its debut sometime in October next year as part of the Fall 2027 anime slate. It’s set to feature a returning staff from the previous seasons with Tomoya Kitagawa returning as director for Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End Season 3 for Madhouse with Tomomi Suzuki handling the composition , Maru Takase and Keisuke Kojima providing the character designs, and Evan Call composing the music.

The voice cast from the first two seasons are confirmed to reprise their respective roles as well, but potential new additions to the cast have yet to be revealed as of this time. Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End Season 3 is also poised to tackle the Golden Land Arc , which is the biggest arc in the series to date as Frieren and the others face off against their strongest demon opponent yet.

How do you feel about Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End ‘s manga being on hiatus for such a long time? Are you going to seek out the new spinoff? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: Duel Masters Pure PLAY'S Manga Ends on November 30
content:
Shogakukan 's Weekly CoroCoro Comic platform will publish the final chapter of the Duel Masters Pure PLAY'S manga, based on the Duel Masters PLAY'S smartphone game, on November 30.

The manga launched on Weekly CoroCoro Comic on September 14. Reki Yayoi is drawing the manga. Hirokuni Nojima - Takara Tomy 's art director, character designer, and story writer for Duel Masters PLAY'S - is credited for the manga's original story and supervision.

The CoroCoro Comic manga website announced on November 18 that Hiroki Kikuzuma and Daisuke Kawasaki 's Duel Masters GT manga will continue in a new arc. Duel Masters GT3 -Glitch of the Twin Heart- , the third part of the series, ended on the same day, after launching on Weekly CoroCoro Comic on August 6.

The first part of the Duel Masters GT manga, Duel Masters GT -Gear of the Twin heart- , launched in August 2025, and ended in October 2025. The second part, Duel Masters GT2 -Gate of the Teleport- , launched in December 2025, and ended on February 26.

Yō Kanebayashi and Shigenobu Matsumoto 's Duel Masters LOST Tsuioku no Suishō ( Duel Masters LOST: Crystal of Remembrance) manga launched in February 2024 and ended in March 2024. Kanebayashi and Matsumoto then launched the Duel Masters LOST ~Gekka no Shinigami~ ( Duel Masters LOST: Reaper of the Moon) manga in August 2024, and ended it in February 2025. Duel Masters LOST ~Bōkyaku no Taiyō~ , the third part of the manga, debuted in September 2025. Duel Masters LOST ~Danzai no Shōnen~ (The Sentencing Boy), the fourth part , debuted on March 26, and ended on July 2. The final chapter revealed the manga would have a fifth part titled Shitsuraku no Duel , which started on September 17.
